subject: Dedicated pool SLA — routing safeguards, queueing behavior, and amendment
body:
From: Maria Velasquez <maria.velasquez@novaedge.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated pool SLA request / routing safeguards and queueing behavior

Hi Karthik and Ben,

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. As we evaluate Redwood for a reserved GPU commitment, we need clearer contractual language around queueing behavior and fallback routing for sustained spikes. Our procurement team put together the attached request (novaedge_dedicated_sla_request.pdf) with the asks summarized below: 

- Target availability: 99.95% monthly for dedicated pool (production model).
- Tail latency objective: p95 <= 200ms for seq=128 on provisioned capacity; p99 target and credit triggers to be defined.
- Queueing behavior: guaranteed queue depth for tenant isolation during peak windows (i.e., soft cap on cross-tenant batching at 10 concurrent inflight requests per reserved GPU until headroom replenishes).
- Preemption & fallback: explicit description of what happens when pool is congested — automated fallback to a lower-cost compatible model variant (quantized or smaller architecture) with defined latency/quality tradeoffs and an SLA-exception credit formula.
- Credits & remedies: formula for credits when dedicated throughput or latency targets are missed, and a 72-hour remediation window before escalation to credits.

We'd like a written amendment to the Master Services Agreement that covers these items and an operations playbook describing runbook steps your SREs will take during congestion. Can you get us a draft amendment and an internal runbook we can review? Procurement needs a redline by May 10 to keep our Q2 budget cadence.

Best,
Maria Velasquez
Head of Platform Engineering
NovaEdge

---
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Maria Velasquez <maria.velasquez@novaedge.com>, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool SLA request / routing safeguards and queueing behavior

Maria — thanks for the clear summary and the attachment. We're aligned on the priority here. I’ll loop in our infra and SRE leads to draft the amendment language and a short runbook. A couple quick clarifying questions before we draft: 

1) For the p95/p99 targets — is NovaEdge comfortable defining the targets against token-level steady-state generation (i.e., excluding cold-cache first request penalties) or do you want the SLO to be measured end-to-end including cold starts?
2) Do you want the fallback behavior to be automatic (system routes to compatible variant when queueing threshold breached) or controlled (manual failover by Redwood SRE/ops after alarm triggers)?

I'll attach a skeleton mutual action plan with milestones (MAP) and propose a draft amendment in 48 hours.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

Attachment: MAP_NovaEdge_timeline.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

---
From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool SLA request / routing safeguards and queueing behavior (internal)

Karthik/Ben — putting down a technical proposal for the amendment and the runbook. High-level decisions and suggested wording below. I’ve attached a runbook draft (runbook_dedicated-fallback.md).

Summary of proposed behavior (recommended):
- Measurement basis: SLOs measured on post-auth request latency at the proxy edge, excluding cold-cache first-token penalty window (30s per model instance warmup). Makes p95/p99 stable.
- Availability definition: monthly uptime measured for the dedicated pool's control plane (orchestration + scheduling) plus per-model worker health; define monthly uptime as (total seconds - down seconds)/total seconds. Target suggested: 99.9% for control plane, 99.95% for per-model serving when pool headroom >= configured baseline.
- Queueing policy: tenant isolation via 'soft inflight cap' — by default allow up to 12 concurrent inflight requests per reserved GPU for the tenant. If overall pool congestion crosses 80% of promised throughput, routing will honor isolation caps and queue at the tenant level with FIFO within tenant. Cross-tenant batching will be throttled progressively rather than abruptly.
- Headroom & burst credits: provision an 'elastic headroom' of X tokens-per-second equivalent (we can map to GPU slots). Customers can draw on burst credits for short spikes up to configured burst duration (e.g. 5 minutes) before fallbacks trigger. We propose a replenishment schedule and a small monthly burst budget in the amendment.
- Preemption & automatic fallback: automated routing to a compatible quantized variant (same architecture, 8-bit quantized or smaller embedding dimension) once sustained queueing > threshold for T minutes (we recommend 2 minutes sustained at queue depth > 75% of tenant cap). The fallback variant must be verified for functional compatibility; degradation profiles will be included in the runbook.
- Credits formula (draft language): if p95 or availability target is missed for a calendar month, credit = min(10% of monthly reserved fee, proportional to minutes below SLO weighted by severity). Provide a 72-hour remediation/mitigation window during which Redwood will attempt to restore service; credits apply after remediation window if issue persists.

Operational runbook highlights (from runbook_dedicated-fallback.md):
1) Alerting thresholds and ownership (on-call SRE + account engineer)
2) Automated routing rules and telemetry to surface cross-tenant interference
3) Manual escalation steps and customer communication templates
4) Post-incident review and credit calculation method

Open items for negotiation with NovaEdge: exact numbers for burst budget, the p99 trigger threshold, and the language around automatic vs manual failover (customers sometimes prefer manual for quality-sensitive inference).

I’ve kept the proposed amendment language intentionally prescriptive to avoid ambiguity in operational expectations. If you want, I can mark options A/B for automatic vs manual fallback and leave a placeholder in the amendment.

-Irene
Irene Choi
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachment: runbook_dedicated-fallback.md (text stub)

---
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Maria Velasquez <maria.velasquez@novaedge.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 08:33:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed amendment & playbook for dedicated pool — NDG-4821

Maria — attached is an initial amendment (redwood_dedicated_amendment_v1.pdf) summarizing the proposed SLOs and the operational commitments, plus the internal runbook we referenced. Key points in plain language: 

- Measurement: p95 computed on warmed requests at the edge; cold-start window excluded (30s).
- Availability & credits: we propose 99.95% monthly availability for the dedicated serving layer when pool headroom >= baseline, with the credit formula Irene outlined.
- Queueing & tenant isolation: soft inflight cap of 12 per reserved GPU with progressive throttling and per-tenant FIFO within queue.
- Burst credits: NovaEdge receives a monthly burst pool (configurable) to cover short spikes; we detailed replenishment mechanics in section 3.
- Fallback behavior: default is automated fallback to a verified quantized variant after T=2 minutes sustained high queueing (we included an opt-out clause if NovaEdge wants manual failover).
- Scheduled maint windows: regular maintenance windows will be notified 7 days in advance; emergency maintenance language is included.

Links: DocuSign for amendment: https://docusign.net/NDG-4821-amendment
Confluence runbook: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/ENG/Dedicated+Fallback+Playbook

If this looks good as a starting point, I can send the amendment for countersignature with our legal team and set up a short call to walk through the tradeoffs (30 minutes). We should also capture NovaEdge's desired burst budget number — I put a placeholder at 10% of committed throughput but can adjust.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_dedicated_amendment_v1.pdf (pdf)

From: Maria Velasquez <maria.velasquez@novaedge.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@novaedge.com
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed amendment & playbook for dedicated pool — NDG-4821

Karthik,

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the level of detail. Procurement reviewed the draft and provided a redlined SOW (attached: redlined_sow_novaedge.pdf). A few immediate redlines: 

- We want p99 included as a secondary target with a clear credit trigger at p99 > 1.2s for more than 30 minutes aggregated per month.
- The burst budget placeholder is insufficient for our traffic profile; we propose starting at 25% of committed throughput for 10 minutes rolling windows.
- We request that automatic fallback be opt-in (i.e., do not switch automatically; require explicit approval or a manual trigger from our on-call unless a production outage is detected).

Can we schedule a 30-minute call to resolve the remaining open items and finalize numbers? Is May 7 at 10:00 AM PT available? Procurement will attend.

Best,
Maria Velasquez
Head of Platform Engineering
NovaEdge

Attachment: redlined_sow_novaedge.pdf (pdf)

Maria — thanks for the redlines. May 7 at 10:00 AM PT works for our team. I’ve sent a calendar invite and included a brief agenda: 1) p99 trigger and credit thresholds, 2) burst budget sizing and replenishment, 3) automatic vs manual fallback options and opt-in language.

Look forward to resolving this.

Karthik Iyer
